rationale: The Court reverses the Fourth Circuit’s near-categorical combat-zone displacement and holds that Boyle-style federal common-law preemption requires a claim-specific showing that the asserted state-law duty significantly conflicts with identifiable military directives or necessarily entails adjudicating hostilities-integral military judgments. Likely separate writings include a Kavanaugh dissent (possibly joined by Thomas/Alito) emphasizing litigation-process intrusion, and one or more concurrences (especially Gorsuch/Barrett) stressing limits on free-ranging federal common law and the text of § 2680(j).
